title: British Raj
capsule: The British Raj was the period of direct Crown rule over India from 1858, when the East India Company's authority was transferred to Queen Victoria following the suppression of the 1857 Uprising, to 1947 when independence and partition created the dominions of India and Pakistan. At its administrative apex the Raj governed British India (provinces under direct rule) alongside some 565 Princely States held under subsidiary alliance, covering the entire subcontinent as well as Burma (until 1937) and Aden. The 1943 Bengal Famine, the Quit India Movement of 1942, and mounting post-World War II pressure led the Attlee government to announce a transfer of power; Mountbatten's partition plan of June 1947 and the Indian Independence Act ended the Raj on 14–15 August 1947.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. British Raj boundaries are among the best-documented in the dataset, based on the Survey of India's systematic triangulation and published Imperial Gazetteers; Princely State internal boundaries are precisely known, though some tribal frontier zones (NWFP, Baluchistan) had only approximate administrative lines.
